title: 7 MID 1800'S FRENCH TRANSFER P...
reason: Eight antique French transfer-printed assiettes parlantes (one more than the title states), two hand-coloured, a collected category; likely $150-350 as a lot.
findings: Eight French transfer-printed earthenware plates are pictured (eight close-ups), not seven as the title says. Captions read: Jamais je n'aime qu'un jour; Apres le Diner; La Lecture; Le Bailli du Village (four black stipple-style transfers with lacy or floral borders, probably 1840s); la botte de ... (last word unclear, looks like Jone or Jour) and Aye Dada (both with hand-coloured centres and painted yellow and blue floral scroll borders, probably 1840s-50s); Droleries, 'Comment! ce lievre ose me demander mon permis de chasse! Quel toupet!' N:6 (black transfer in a red-pink floral border, probably later 19th century); Le Langage des Fleurs, 5. Le Laurier, Gloire (black transfer with a blue border showing soldiers in kepis, probably c.1880-1900). These are assiettes parlantes or histoire-type plates of the kind made by Creil et Montereau, Choisy-le-Roi and similar French factories, a collected category. No backstamps are photographed (only the plate fronts), so makers are unconfirmed, and the mid-1800s date fits about six of the eight.
condition: Crazing, wear to gilt rims on the grey plates and scattered small brown spots in the glaze; the pink-border plate has orange-brown staining at the rim. No cracks, chips or rivets obvious in the photos, but backs and rims are not photographed.
rescore_note: Eight genuine 19th century French transfer-printed assiettes parlantes (two hand-coloured), a collected niche, but makers unconfirmed, crazing and staining and no backs shown; French sellers ask about EUR 30 to 40 for similar plates (leboncoin.fr/ck/collection/faience, seen 19/10/2026), so my estimate is $130 to $240 for the lot.
